caption_used: Comparison of per-output and per-layer perplexity at different sparsity rates using a logarithmic scale. Both pruning configurations maintain comparable perplexity below 10^1 for sparsity rates up to 50%, after which values begin to diverge. At 60% sparsity, the Per-Output configuration reaches approximately 15 while Per-Layer remains near 10^1. The most pronounced separation occurs at 70%, where Per-Output perplexity climbs to roughly 50 while Per-Layer reaches approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both configurations approach 10^3, with Per-Output exhibiting marginally higher perplexity than Per-Layer at this extreme.

The "Per-Layer" series begins at a similar level around 1 at 10% sparsity, increasing to approximately 25 at 80% sparsity. The bars are not visually emphasized with any special formatting such as shading or borders.
raw_responses.Chinese:
The figure presents a comparison of perplexity values for two configurations, "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer," across varying sparsity rates. The chart type is a grouped bar graph. The horizontal axis, labeled "Sparsity Rate," displays sparsity rates ranging from 10% to 80%, incrementing by 10% intervals. The vertical axis, labeled "Perplexity," uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, and 10^2, and 10^3. The data is presented in grouped bars, with each sparsity rate having two bars representing the "Per-Output" and "Per-Layer" configurations. The "Per-Output" configuration is represented by blue bars, while the "Per-Layer" configuration is represented by orange bars. The bars are arranged side-by-side for each sparsity rate. At 10% sparsity, both configurations have bars with approximate heights of 2. At 20% sparsity, both bars are approximately 2. At 30% sparsity, both bars are approximately 3. At 40% sparsity, both bars are approximately 3. At 50% sparsity, the "Per-Output" bar is approximately 4, while the "Per-Layer" bar is approximately 3. At 60% sparsity, the "Per-Output" bar reaches approximately 15, while the "Per-Layer" bar is approximately 10. At 70% sparsity, the "Per-Output" bar reaches approximately 50, while the "Per-Layer" bar is approximately 25. At 80% sparsity, both bars approach a height of 1000. The bars are not sorted in any particular order beyond the order of the sparsity rates. No bars are visually emphasized.
